hints: Interpret each modulus inequality geometrically as a distance condition on the Argand plane.
The condition $|z-2|\leq1$ is the closed disc with centre $(2,0)$ and radius $1$.
For $|z-(1-2i)|\leq|z|$, draw the perpendicular bisector of the segment from $(0,0)$ to $(1,-2)$ and select the side containing $(1,-2)$.
Shade only the overlap of that half-plane with the closed disc, keeping both boundary curves solid.
walkthrough: Show the relevant part of a circle of radius $1$; follow through a centre not at the origin even if it is incorrectly placed at $1-2i$, and it must clearly pass through $(1,0)$ or $(3,0)$ (or the corresponding points for follow through)
Show the point representing $1-2i$; this may be implied by the correct perpendicular bisector

Show the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $1-2i$ to the origin, perpendicular by eye and through the midpoint by eye; it must reach the midpoint and, if extended, cut the stated circle boundaries

Shade the correct region, dependent on all earlier marks except in the printed no-scale case. The scheme permits scale implied by dashes and lists three scale cases, with the final shading mark available in each if the construction relationships are correct
The intersection of the closed disc centred at $(2,0)$ with radius $1$ and the half-plane $y\le\frac12x-\frac54$.
